questions.cardText:
[Psychology] Laughing has been observed to:
A. Alter pain perception based on the context
B. Briefly amplify one’s perception of pain due to sensory overload
C. Raise a person’s threshold for pain
Answer: C. Laughter can increase pain tolerance by releasing endorphins, which are natural painkillers produced by the brain.
questions.en: What effect has laughing been observed to have on a person's pain threshold, through the endorphins the brain releases?
questions.de: Welche Wirkung hat Lachen nachweislich auf die Schmerzschwelle eines Menschen, durch die Endorphine, die das Gehirn dabei ausschüttet?

timeline.labelEn: Dunbar et al. publish 'Social laughter is correlated with an elevated pain threshold'
timeline.labelDe: Dunbar et al. veröffentlichen die Studie, dass gemeinsames Lachen mit einer erhöhten Schmerzschwelle einhergeht

questions.notes: Source: Dunbar et al. (2011, Proc. R. Soc. B), cited on the Laughter article; the laughter-related endorphin release raised pain thresholds (pain tolerance).

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Inventions] What was the original purpose of the chainsaw?
A. Assisting in childbirth
B. Sculpting ice
C. Cutting down trees
Answer: A. The chainsaw was originally invented in the late 18th century to aid in difficult childbirths.
questions.en: For what medical purpose was the chainsaw originally invented in the late 18th century?
questions.de: Zu welchem medizinischen Zweck wurde die Kettensäge ursprünglich im späten 18. Jahrhundert erfunden?

timeline.labelEn: Scottish doctors John Aitken and James Jeffray devise the chain 'flexible saw' for surgery
timeline.labelDe: Die schottischen Ärzte John Aitken und James Jeffray entwickeln die kettenförmige „flexible Säge“ für die Chirurgie

questions.notes: Aitken's chain saw (c. 1783–1785) was for symphysiotomy in obstructed childbirth; Jeffray used it for excising diseased bone.
